long_biography.plain_text:
At 18, José Luis Díaz-Varela left Galicia for Venezuela, where work as a medical representative led him into Heinz Kern’s chemical-distribution business. Kern made the young salesman his deputy and backed his proposal to open a Spanish operation. Díaz-Varela founded Industrial Kern Española in Barcelona in 1962, later bought out his partner and became sole owner.

He reinvested profits to expand the business internationally, created animal-health company Calier and later established Kern Pharma after acquiring a Roche plant. The group evolved from chemical and pharmaceutical ingredients into human medicines, generic drugs, vaccines and veterinary products. Díaz-Varela retained the chairmanship while transferring daily management to his children, preserving a family-controlled healthcare group after the sale of its original chemical-distribution arm.
